item.title: Tinubu wants gas resources to improve Nigerians’ lives – Ekpo
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas), Hon. Ekperikpe Ekpo, has said President Bola Tinubu wants Nigeria’s abundant gas resources to translate into better living conditions for Nigerians. Ekpo spoke on Tuesday in Kano during the commissioning of two Liquefied Compressed Natural Gas (LCNG) facilities developed by Rolling Energy with support from the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF). He said the projects demonstrated the Federal Government’s commitment to turning its gas policies into practical infrastructure that would improve access to domestic gas. “The President has been unequivocal that Nigeria’s abundant gas resources must translate into real improvements in the lives of our people,” he said. The minister said the facilities would expand gas supply in Kano and neighbouring areas, provide cleaner energy alternatives, support businesses and transportation, and create economic opportunities. He explained that the Tamburawa distribution hub has LNG storage, regasification and CNG distribution facilities, while the retail outlets would bring gas closer to consumers. Ekpo also stressed the importance of private sector investment in developing the gas industry. According to him, government must go beyond making policies to providing infrastructure that benefits Nigerians. “Government cannot stop at formulating good policies. We must catalyse the private capital and infrastructure required to translate those policies into benefits that Nigerians can see, use and feel,” he said. Also speaking, the Executive Chairman of the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles (Pi-CNG), Barrister Ismaeel Ahmed, said the expansion of refuelling stations would make cheaper and cleaner transportation more accessible to Nigerians. Ahmed, who was represented by his Special Adviser on Technical Training and Capacity Building, Mr Omoh Imoukhede, said the growth of CNG infrastructure must go hand in hand with vehicle conversions. “The conversation about energy transition cannot remain about what Nigeria can do with its enormous gas resources. Nigerians must begin to see the infrastructure, use the infrastructure and experience the benefits in their lives every day,” he said. He described Kano as an important location for CNG expansion because of its large transport sector and commercial activities, adding that more refuelling stations would encourage drivers and transport operators to switch to gas. “Conversion without refuelling infrastructure will not deliver the transition we want. The two must grow together,” he said. Ahmed commended the MDGIF, Rolling Energy and the Kano State Government for supporting the development of the facilities. He also urged stakeholders to prioritise affordability, availability and safety. In his remarks, the Kano State Commissioner for Power and Renewable Energy, Engr. item.title: Makinde Presents ₦1.115tn 2027 Budget To Oyo Assembly
item.description: Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has presented a proposed budget of ₦1.115 trillion for the 2027 fiscal year to the State House of Assembly for consideration and approval. Tagged the “Budget of Sustained Progress”, the proposal is valued at ₦1,115,341,378,359.90. Presenting the budget on Tuesday at the Assembly complex in Agodi, Ibadan, Makinde said it was designed to consolidate the gains of his administration and lay a foundation for sustainable development beyond its tenure. He described it as the final budget proposal of his administration, saying it would sustain the state’s development momentum and ensure continuity after the transition to a new government. “As we prepare to hand over the baton to the next administration, we bring before you the 2027 Budget of Sustained Progress. It is designed to consolidate our gains, sustain public services and carry our state’s development forward through the transition period and beyond,” he said. The governor said the proposal prioritised infrastructure, community development and the strengthening of public institutions, with significant allocations for capital projects in health, education and road infrastructure. He added that his administration was committed to leaving behind clear records, properly documented processes and institutions capable of sustaining efficient service delivery. Highlighting his administration’s achievements, Makinde said Oyo State’s Internally Generated Revenue increased by 288 per cent, from ₦26.59 billion in 2019 to ₦103.25 billion in 2025. He also noted that the state ranked third nationally in the 2025 Subnational Ease of Doing Business Assessment. The governor said targeted interventions and partnerships had helped return about 65,000 out-of-school children to classrooms, alongside investments in educational infrastructure, recruitment and service delivery. He, however, said the administration’s performance should be measured beyond revenue figures and rankings. “Figures alone cannot fully assess our administration. The real measure of success is the impact we have made on the lives of our people and the institutions we have built to serve them beyond May 29, 2027,” he said. Makinde also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to women’s inclusion in governance, pledging to sustain the 35 per cent affirmative action policy for women. On infrastructure and agriculture, he said the government had prioritised strategic road projects to connect economic corridors, improve market access and create opportunities for farmers, businesses and rural communities. He said the establishment of the Oyo State Agribusiness Development Agency had helped reposition agriculture as a viable business sector, while the Oyo State Agribusiness Transformation Centre had become a hub for agricultural investment. According to him, the centre hosts 16 agribusinesses with investments valued at more than ₦20 billion, while over 30,000 farmers have been captured in the state’s agricultural datab

item.title: Sanwo-Olu appoints Akinyemi as acting MD LAWMA
item.description: .Reviews management structure By Olasunkanmi Akoni Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu has finally appointed Olajuwon Akinyemi as the acting Managing Director of the Lagos State Waste Management Authority, LAWMA. By the appointment, Akinyemi succeeded former M.D, Dr. Muyiwa Gbadegesin who was forced to resign following intractable waste management challenges across the state. When contacted, the state Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, on Tuesday evening, confirmed the appointment. According to Wahab, the new MD, who was the former Executive Director of Operations, will also serve in the capacity of Executive Director, Finance. Also, in the coming days, new officers would be redeployed in the restructuring effort of the management staff. This comes following reports of forced resignation of former M.D, Dr. Muyiwa Gbadegesin over the seemingly intractable waste management challenges across the state. This laid to rest earlier reported appointment of , Dr. Hassan Sanuth, Director Sanitation Services – Office of Environment in the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources as acting MD. However, Sanuth was temporarily drafted to LAWMA to assist in waste management pending appointment of substantive managing director. On October 19, indications emerged that Governor Sanwo-Olu has directed Gbadegesin to resign amid persistent refuse accumulation across the state. It was gathered that the governor became increasingly dissatisfied with Gbadegesin’s handling of the waste management crisis and had asked him to step down. Earlier in September 2026, during an inspection of the Olusosun Dumpsite in Ojota, Sanwo-Olu handed a strong warning against further failure to stop the menace announcing plans to overhaul the agency for effective management, describing Gbadegesin’s inability as “sabotage” According to an inside source, “the governor’s displeasure stemmed from the slow pace of waste evacuation and the alleged failure of Gbadegesin to act promptly on directives aimed at addressing the crisis. “The governor was at the Olusosun Dumpsite in Ojota a month ago and was dissatisfied with the state of things. He gave instructions that immediate action be taken on the matter, as he has declared a state of emergency on waste management. “The governor was upset when he observed that the situation had not improved despite his clear directive. So, over the weekend, he asked him to resign, although he is begging and has reached out to some prominent Lagosians to beg on his behalf.” Also, residents across Lagos have repeatedly complained about worsening waste collection, with refuse accumulating along road medians, streets and major highways. The prevalent parts of the state, include: Ogba, Idimu, Ejigbo, Mushin, Egbeda, Surulere, Ajegunle, Ikorodu, Ojo, Obalende, Apapa and Mile 2, where residents have had to contend with heaps of stinking refuse along streets and drainage channels. item.title: Embrace HIV testing as routine healthcare-Lagos govt urges residents
item.description: . Extends free screening to staff, trade fair visitors By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has urged residents across the state to embrace HIV testing as part of routine healthcare rather than wait until they suspect an infection before seeking screening. Meanwhile, the state government has extended free HIV testing and counselling services to public servants and visitors to the ongoing 2026 International Trade Fair as part of efforts to promote early diagnosis and expand access to HIV prevention and treatment. The interventions, implemented by the Lagos State AIDS Control Agency (LSACA), are aimed at bringing HIV-related services closer to residents, encouraging routine testing and ensuring that individuals who require further care are linked to appropriate treatment facilities. At the Public Service Week health screening exercise, the Head of Service, Lagos State, Mr Bode Agoro, officially opened the free screening programme and urged public servants to prioritise their health by taking advantage of the opportunity. Agoro said access to preventive healthcare, including HIV screening, was essential to building a healthy, productive and efficient workforce. He encouraged workers to embrace regular health checks and utilise the confidential testing, professional counselling and information on HIV prevention, transmission and treatment provided through the exercise. In a related intervention, LSACA commenced free HIV testing and counselling services at the Lagos Pavilion, Tafawa Balewa Square (TBS), as part of activities at the 2026 International Trade Fair. The exercise, which began on Friday, November 6, is scheduled to run for 10 days, ending on Sunday, November 15. It provides visitors, exhibitors, traders and other participants with access to confidential HIV screening, counselling, preventive health information and guidance on accessing treatment and care where necessary. The Chief Executive Officer of LSACA, Dr Folakemi Animashaun, reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to ensuring that HIV prevention, testing and treatment services remain accessible, confidential and free from discrimination. Animashaun said knowing one’s HIV status was an important step towards preventing new infections and improving health outcomes, noting that early diagnosis enables individuals who test positive to commence treatment promptly and maintain healthy, productive lives. She urged public servants, Trade Fair participants and residents across the state to embrace HIV testing as part of routine healthcare rather than wait until they suspect an infection before seeking screening. The LSACA chief executive also emphasised the importance of collaboration with Ministries, Departments and Agencies, development partners, civil society organisations and other stakeholders in expanding access to HIV prevention, testing, treatment and care services. item.title: ‎States must contribute to pension protection fund to benefit from minimum pension — PenCom DG
item.description: ‎–It is big shame for some state retirees to be paid ₦5,000’ ‎‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎‎ABUJA — The Director-General of Nigeria’s National Pension Commission (PenCom), Ms. Omolola Bridget Oloworaran, said on Tuesday that states must contribute to the Pension Protection Fund before they can become eligible for the minimum pension. ‎‎She stated this at the official launch of the Minimum Pension Guarantee Scheme and the unveiling of PenCare, a pension industry-funded healthcare initiative designed to provide low-income retirees with access to essential medical services free of charge. ‎‎The event was held at the Old Banquet Hall, Presidential Villa, Abuja. ‎She said about 170,000 retirees are expected to receive the minimum pension of ₦52,500, including those who were previously receiving less than that amount. ‎‎“Every eligible retiree who earns below ₦52,500 will be uplifted to ₦52,500. So, of course, as I said, there is no discrimination if you are within the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS). ‎‎“However, there is an eligibility criterion at the same level. We are making it a requirement that states must contribute to the Pension Protection Fund before they can be eligible for the minimum pension. ‎‎“So, we will work out that modality at the state level because we all know that the fund needs to be sustainable. If people are not contributing, we will run out of funds, and we cannot start a laudable initiative like this and then, years from now, somebody says it has stopped working because people are not contributing. ‎‎“So, we are working on modalities for the states to start contributing. But, as of now, it does not apply only to federal workers. Even private-sector workers are receiving these minimum pensions. ‎‎“As I said in my speech, 54 per cent of the total number of retirees who fall below the minimum pension work in the private sector, even though the private sector is not the majority employer. Essentially, 65 per cent or more of private-sector retirees are earning less than ₦52,500. ‎‎“So, when we tell them to contribute to the Pension Protection Fund, there is a reason for that. They form a large chunk of the money we need.” ‎‎On whether anything was being done to ensure that retirees from states also benefit from the minimum pension, as some of them still receive about ₦5,000 monthly, the PenCom DG said it was shameful to pay someone such an amount, although she doubted whether any state actually paid such a paltry sum. ‎‎“Frankly, that is a big shame. What we have done is that we have started working with the states to ensure that they pay retirement benefits to their retirees and also put a plan in place to review pensionable inflation. ‎‎“I mean, receiving ₦5,000 is unacceptable. I do hope it is not true. I will ask my team to confirm. ‎‎“But ultimately, what we are trying to do is get all the states into the scheme. item.title: Awujale stool: Adele-in-Council sues Abiodun, challenges reconstituted interregnum committee
item.description: By James Ogunnaike Abeokuta The Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council has dragged the Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, and members of the reconstituted Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council before the state High Court, Ijebu-Ode, challenging what it described as an unlawful attempt to displace the traditional administrative structure of Ijebuland. Other defendants sued alongside Gov Abiodun are the Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs as well as members of the recently reconstituted Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council including High Chief Rasheed Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu Ode, Chief Chris Okunowo, the Bobasuwa, Prof Jide Ajayi, the Jagun Aso, Chief Stephen Bakare, the Babalaje as well as Chief Alade Shote, the Otun Balogun The suit dated November 5, 2026 and marked HCJ/201/2026 according to a statement from the Media office of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council and supporting court documents made available to journalists on Tuesday seeks to establish the authority of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council to oversee the traditional and administrative affairs of Ijebu-Ode during the interregnum following the transition of the late Awujale of Ijebuland, Oba Sikiru Kayode Adetona. The nine members of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council led by the Adele and Ogbeni Oja of Ijebuland, Olorogun Dr Sonny Kuku, are asking the court to declare that the Adele system is the only legitimate traditional administrative authority recognised by the native law, customs and ancestral practices of the Ijebu people during the period between the reigns of successive Awujales. They are also challenging the establishment and subsequent reconstitution of the Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council, describing the arrangement as alien to Ijebu customary law and inconsistent with the Ogun State Chiefs Law. In the substantive suit, the plaintiffs are seeking a declaration that neither the state governor nor the relevant government authorities possess the power to create or reconstitute an administrative council capable of displacing the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council during an interregnum. They are further asking the court to set aside the purported reconstitution of the AIAC and the appointments of the fifth to eighth defendants, describing the appointments as irregular, illegal, unconstitutional, null and void. The plaintiffs also want a perpetual injunction restraining the governor, the relevant ministries and other government officials from interfering with or bypassing the customary administrative functions of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council. Similarly, they are seeking an order restraining the reconstituted Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council from holding meetings, parading themselves or exercising traditional, civil or financial administrative authority over Ijebu-Ode under the disputed AIAC arrangement. item.title: Only Rainbow Coalition can guarantee Tinubu’s victory in Bayelsa – PDP
item.description: By Emem Idio, Yenagoa The Peoples Democratic Party ,PDP, in Bayelsa State has claimed that the Rainbow Coalition is central to President Bola Tinubu’s re-election prospects in the state, pledging to mobilise 300,000 votes for the President in the 2027 general elections. The state PDP chairman and leader of the coalition, Chief George Alabh Turnah, made the declaration in a statement issued by his Senior Special Assistant on Media and Communication, Kevin Loveday-Egbo. Turnah said the coalition would take its campaign for Tinubu’s re-election to communities across the state, with a grassroots mobilisation strategy targeting undecided voters ahead of the 2027 elections. He described the National Rainbow Coalition as a platform for engaging voters, explaining that the group would use its community-level outreach to highlight what it considers the achievements of the Tinubu administration and canvass support for his second term. The PDP chairman said the coalition was committed to expanding its mobilisation network across the state, adding that its target was to secure 300,000 votes for the President. He also challenged the All Progressives Congress, APC, to mobilise an additional 500,000 votes, bringing the combined target of both parties to 800,000 votes. “The Rainbow Coalition has pledged 300,000 votes for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in Bayelsa State. We are tasking the APC to deliver 500,000 votes to bring the total number of votes for the APC to 800,000 out of the one million, one hundred and fifty thousand Permanent Voter Cards collected in the state,” Turnah said. He said the coalition would intensify its grassroots engagements across Bayelsa as preparations gather momentum for the 2027 general elections. item.title: Three feared killed as gunmen attack mining site in Plateau
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – No fewer than three persons have reportedly been killed following an attack by gunmen on a mining site in Jol community, Riyom Local Government Area of Plateau State. The incident occurred at about 6pm on Tuesday, when the assailants reportedly stormed the mining site and opened fire on people in the area. A resident of the community, Bulus Shen, who confirmed the incident, told newsmen that the gunmen arrived at the mining site in the evening and began shooting sporadically. Shen said the attack threw the community into panic, adding that three persons were reportedly killed in the incident. The spokesperson of the Berom Youth Moulders Association (BYM), Rwang Tengwong, also confirmed the attack. Tengwong condemned the killing, describing the incident as disturbing and unacceptable. He called on security agencies to urgently investigate the attack, apprehend those responsible and strengthen security around rural communities to prevent further loss of lives. Efforts to get further details from security operatives were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. item.title: Abia 2027: Agbazuere makes U-turn, backs Otti’s 2nd term bid
item.description: . Dismisses Ogbonnaya’s alleged anti-Ngwa claim, warns critics By Steve Oko UMUAHIA—Former Chief of Staff to ex-Governor Okezie Ikpeazu, Prof. ACB Agbazuere, who strongly opposed Governor Alex Otti during the 2019 governorship election, has thrown his weight behind the governor’s re-election bid, declaring that he deserves a second term. Agbazuere, now a member of Otti’s Campaign Advisory Council, also dismissed allegations credited to former Commissioner, Chief Charles Ogbonnaya, that the governor allegedly described Ngwa people as brainless, describing the claim as unfounded and politically motivated. Speaking during a radio interview simulcast across several stations in Abia on Tuesday, Agbazuere warned politicians against making unsubstantiated allegations, saying defamatory statements could attract civil and criminal consequences under Nigerian laws, including the Cybercrimes Act. He said the allegation posed no threat to Otti’s political support base, particularly among the Ngwa people. “Dr Alex Otti may love peace; Dr Alex Otti may not want trouble, but they should see that people like us are now with him. Anybody who wants to say anything should be careful and say what he knows to be true,” he warned. Explaining his support for the governor, Agbazuere said Otti’s administration had demonstrated commitment to infrastructure development, urban renewal, workers’ welfare and good governance. He cited the reconstruction of Port Harcourt Road and Bank Road in Aba, the Omenuko Bridge and Arochukwu Road as evidence of the administration’s infrastructure drive. He also commended the governor for regular payment of salaries, pensions and gratuities, as well as improvements in traditional rulers’ allowances. On criticisms that increased federal allocations should have translated into more projects, Agbazuere argued that the rising cost of construction materials must be considered, citing the increase in cement prices from about N2,000 to N12,000 per bag. He challenged critics to visit the state and assess ongoing projects rather than judge the administration from a distance. Describing Otti as a banker and trained economist, he said the governor understood accountability and prudent management of public resources. Agbazuere urged Abians to look beyond party affiliations and support continuity, arguing that a second term would enable Otti to complete ongoing projects and consolidate his administration’s programmes. He recalled that even during the 2023 election, a leading opposition governorship candidate had reportedly acknowledged Otti as the best candidate. Vanguard reports that Agbazuere, a former Commissioner for Information, was among Otti’s vocal critics but recently switched allegiance after dumping the All Progressives Congress (APC), where he briefly sought political shelter shortly after Otti assumed office in 2023. item.title: 2027: Avoid technicalities, treat electronic evidence rigorously, INEC charges tribunals
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Professor Joash Amupitan SAN, has urged members of the 2027 Election Petition Tribunals to avoid technicalities that defeat substantive justice and to subject electronic evidence to rigorous scrutiny. He also told them to keep firm control of their courtrooms and let “truth of the ballot prevail”. According to the commission’s Daily Bulletin of Tuesday, Amupitan spoke on Monday in Abuja while delivering the Commission’s opening remarks at a three-day workshop for Justices of the Court of Appeal and members of the tribunals, held at the Body of Benchers Complex. The Court of Appeal organised the workshop under the theme “Election Tribunal as a Tool for Political Stability.” The INEC chairman said electoral litigation had grown more complex, with disputes now touching on voter accreditation, electronic transmission of results, technological failures and the integrity of digital records. On the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System BVAS and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV), he said technology should neither be treated as infallible nor dismissed simply because the evidence is electronic. Amupitan warned that digital disinformation driven by artificial intelligence, audio cloning and deepfake videos would inevitably spill into the courtrooms. He urged the tribunals to apply strict evidentiary standards under Section 84 of the Evidence Act, saying digital provenance, forensic chain of custody and reliance on certified data from INEC would be vital to stop synthetic fabrications from misleading the courts. He added that electoral adjudication is evidence-driven, and that allegations of irregularities, non-compliance or result manipulation must be proved with credible and legally admissible evidence. According to him, the Commission has issued the Regulations and Guidelines for the Conduct of Elections, 2026, to give clearer operational standards against which claims of non-compliance can be weighed in proceedings. The INEC chairman told the tribunal members that they carry the democratic aspirations of over 200 million Nigerians once they take their oaths. He described the courtroom as the altar on which public confidence in constitutional governance is preserved, and urged them to let their decisions reflect deep fidelity to the law, uncompromising integrity and the principle that justice must be seen to be done. Amupitan said Nigeria’s political stability in 2027 would depend not only on how efficiently INEC conducts elections, but also on how courageously, transparently and justly the tribunals settle the disputes that follow. He described the Election Petition Tribunal as a constitutional valve that releases political pressure and keeps electoral friction from degenerating into civil disruption. item.title: Makinde presents N1.12trn final budget
item.description: …Allocates 60% to capital expenditure …Dismisses appointees’ resignations as meaningless By Adeola Badru Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, on Tuesday presented a proposed N1.12 trillion budget for the 2027 fiscal year to the State House of Assembly, describing it as the “Budget of Sustained Progress”, while dismissing the recent resignations of political appointees as inconsequential. Makinde said the departure of some officials from his administration would not distract his government or affect its commitment to delivering its mandate. The governor made the remarks while presenting the 2027 Appropriation Bill, valued at N1,115,341,378,359.94, before lawmakers at the Parliament Building, Secretariat, Ibadan. Speaking against the backdrop of recent resignations by political appointees and other government officials, Makinde said he was keeping count of those who had left but insisted that their decisions were of no significance to his administration. He also disclosed that one of the female officials who resigned had approached him with what he described as an impossible request, adding that she tendered her resignation after he declined to grant it. The presentation is particularly significant as the proposed estimates represent the final appropriation bill of Makinde’s administration, which is expected to complete its second term in 2027. Under the proposal, capital expenditure accounts for N670.03 billion, representing 60.07 per cent of the total budget, while recurrent expenditure stands at N445.31 billion, or 39.93 per cent. Explaining the allocation, the governor said the proposed spending reflected his administration’s determination to sustain infrastructure development, consolidate existing achievements and strengthen the delivery of essential services across the state. He said about 60 per cent of every N100 provided for in the budget would go into capital investments, stressing that infrastructure remained central to economic growth and long-term prosperity. Makinde, however, cautioned that physical infrastructure alone could not guarantee meaningful development without adequate investment in human resources and essential public services. He said schools needed teachers, hospitals required healthcare professionals, medicines and equipment, while public institutions must be adequately staffed and equipped to function effectively. According to him, the proposed budget was also informed by consultations with stakeholders and residents across the state’s administrative and political zones, whose concerns and expectations shaped the government’s spending priorities. The governor also used the occasion to advocate continuity in governance beyond the expiration of his tenure, unveiling what he called the Omituntun 3.0 agenda. He said the initiative was designed to prevent a reversal of the development trajectory established by his administration over the past seven and a half years after the 2027 governorship election. item.title: Carex Rewards Thousands Of Consumers As Everybody Wins Promo Concludes With Grand Finale Live Draw
item.description: Carex, one of Nigeria’s leading personal hygiene brands, has successfully concluded its nationwide Everybody Wins Promo with a transparent Grand Finale Live Draw, rewarding loyal consumers and reinforcing its commitment to delivering value beyond personal care products. The campaign, which ran from June 2026 to August 2026, attracted millions of consumers PAN Nigeria and rewarded winners with prizes worth over ₦400,000,000. The Grand Finale Live Draw, held in Lagos, brought together consumers, media representatives, trade partners, regulatory officials, and other key stakeholders to witness the selection of the campaign’s grand prize winner through a transparent and independently supervised process. The event marked the culmination of months of consumer participation and engagement, further strengthening the connection between the Carex brand and its consumers. Throughout the promotion, participants had multiple opportunities to win exciting rewards, including instant Recharge Cards, shopping Vouchers, and a brand-new Car. Over 90,000 consumers emerged as winners over the course of the campaign. The grand prize car winner, Faith Stephen from Ijebu Ode, Ogun State, emerged through the live draw process conducted in accordance with all applicable promotional and regulatory requirements. Speaking at the event, Ifunanya Anwunah, Head of Category – Personal Hygiene, said: “At Carex, we believe that the consumers who trust our products every day deserve to be appreciated and rewarded. The Everybody Wins Promo was created as a tangible expression of our gratitude for the loyalty and support we continue to receive from Nigerian families. The overwhelming participation and enthusiasm witnessed throughout this campaign demonstrate the strong connection consumers have with the Carex brand. The promo was built on a simple promise: giving everyday consumers the opportunity to win meaningful rewards while enjoying the quality, care, and protection they have come to trust from Carex. As a brand trusted by millions of Nigerians for their personal hygiene and care needs, Carex remains committed to developing initiatives that deepen consumer engagement, reward loyalty, and create memorable experiences for consumers across the country. The successful completion of the Everybody Wins Promo further underscores the brand’s commitment to putting consumers at the heart of everything it does. ABOUT CAREX Carex is committed to winning the war against germs through a range of antibacterial products that support the health, hygiene, and wellbeing of consumers. Through innovative products and engaging consumer initiatives, Carex continues to build meaningful connections with families across Nigeria, delivering trusted products that help consumers live healthier and more confident lives. item.title: ADC-PCC to Tinubu: Where is the electricity you promised Nigerians?
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has challenged President Bola Tinubu to account for his unfulfilled electricity pledge, accusing him of resorting to personal attacks, divisive rhetoric and recycled promises instead of presenting a credible scorecard of his administration. The Council said Nigerians expected the President to explain what had become of his major campaign promises after nearly three-and-a-half years in office, particularly against the backdrop of worsening insecurity, widespread hunger, rising living costs and massive government borrowings. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC said Tinubu’s recent campaign outings in Kaduna, Rivers and Jigawa states offered little beyond verbal attacks on opponents and familiar promises. Recalling the President’s electricity pledge, the Council challenged him to explain why millions of Nigerians were still struggling with unreliable power supply. “If I don’t give you electricity, don’t vote for me for a second term,” it quoted Tinubu as saying. The ADC-PCC described his renewed electricity promises during the Jigawa campaign as an attempt to repackage an old commitment, adding that the President had reportedly invested in alternative power arrangements for his personal comfort. The Council also questioned the fate of 2,000 tractors reportedly imported from Brazil under the administration’s mechanised farming initiative, alleging that they had yet to make any meaningful impact on agricultural productivity. It further accused Tinubu of taking credit for projects initiated by his predecessor, late President Muhammadu Buhari, insisting that his administration had little of its own to showcase. On the state of democracy, the ADC-PCC accused the President of undermining the independence of democratic institutions, alleging undue influence over the National Assembly and attempts to compromise the Judiciary. item.title: N210trn not missing from NNPC – Mele Kyari tells Senate
item.description: By Henry Umoru – ABUJA The immediate past Group Chief Executive Officer, GCEO, of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company, NNPC, Limited, Mele Kyari has appeared before the Senate, refuting alleged unaccounted N210 trillion in the balance sheet of the National oil company as contained in the 2017 to 2023 Audit report. Kyari who finally appeared before the Senator Ibrahim Dankwabo (PDP, Gombe North) led Senate Committee on Public Accounts said the alleged unaccounted figures arose from accounting entries which have nothing to do with financial loss. He declared that no such financial infraction happened under him as Chief Executive of NNPCL from 2019 to 2025. Kyari said, “I wish to confirm that nothing was lost. It is simply not possible that such an amount could have been lost under my care and leadership. “The matter relates to accounting entries, which have nothing to do with any financial loss. “They are bookkeeping issues, and I believe the appropriate explanations have been provided in my report.” The former NNPCL boss who declared that the N5billion allegedly spent on change of name from NNPC to NNPCL , waa untrue as there was no spending like that under his watch, however refuted queries raised in the audit report on registration and incorporation of NNPC Ltd. He said: “At the time of incorporation, the company was not owned by the Federation in the same manner. “The Federation was therefore responsible for the payment relating to the incorporation of NNPC. “However, NNPC made the payment on behalf of the Federation and subsequently charged it to the Federation’s revenue, which was reflected in what we referred to as the former NAPIMS account of NNPC. “This was simply an accounting entry, involving approximately N2.99 billion. It was a payment made to government institutions responsible for providing the relevant services. “I have also seen comments suggesting that N5 billion was paid for the naming of the company. That is not correct”. According to him, NNPCL under him was transformed from loss incurring corporation to a profit making company, adding that prior to his assumption of office as Group Managing Director of NNPC in 2019 , the national oil company had a huge loss of $803billion in 2018 operational year , which gradually turned to o profit making under him from 2019 . Kyari said, “Mr Chairman, you may be aware from the financial records that the company recorded a loss of about $803billion in 2018. “I took over in 2019, and we did everything possible to transform the company into a profitable organisation which made it to for the first time in its 44 years of existence, recording sustained profits” Satisfied with the submissions of Kyari , the Committee through its Chairman, Senator Dankwabo said , responses submitted to the queries shall be thoroughly studied for final decision on the audit report . item.title: ACF crisis deepens as chairman alleges invasion of secretariat
item.description: — Osuman accuses individuals of breaking into Kaduna headquarters, removing valuables By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The leadership crisis in the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF) has taken a fresh turn following allegations by its National Chairman, Maman Mike Osuman, that some individuals forcibly gained access to the organisation’s national secretariat in Kaduna and removed valuables. In a petition dated November 9, 2026, and addressed to Governor Uba Sani of Kaduna State, Osuman accused two individuals of allegedly breaking into the ACF headquarters at No. 11A Sokoto Road, Kaduna, without the authorisation of the recognised leadership. The petition was also copied to the Inspector-General of Police, the Kaduna State Commissioner of Police and the Director of the Department of State Services (DSS) in the state. According to Osuman, the individuals allegedly gained access to the premises by breaking the gates and office doors, changing the locks and removing valuables and other properties belonging to the organisation. He further alleged that the operation was carried out without the knowledge or consent of the recognised leadership of the forum and without a search warrant. Describing the alleged incident as an assault on the institutional integrity of the organisation, Osuman appealed to Governor Sani to intervene to prevent further escalation of the crisis. “An invasion of this nature not only violates the sanctity of our corporate headquarters but is also a direct assault on the dignity of the entire Northern Region,” he said. The chairman described the national secretariat as the collective heritage of Northern Nigeria, stressing that its protection was essential to preserving the dignity and integrity of the organisation. He urged the governor to use his good offices to ensure that the rule of law prevailed and that the forum was protected against actions capable of undermining its stability. The latest allegation has renewed attention on the protracted leadership crisis within the ACF, particularly the disagreement over control of its national secretariat and the authority to manage the organisation’s affairs. The dispute has been characterised by competing positions among the forum’s leadership organs over the interpretation of its constitution, leadership structure and the legitimacy of decisions taken by the contending sides. In one of the major developments, the National Executive Committee (NEC) of the forum reportedly suspended its Board of Trustees (BoT) Chairman, Alhaji Bashir M. Dalhatu, over alleged violations of the organisation’s constitution. The suspension followed an emergency NEC meeting held in Kaduna in May 2026, amid tensions over access to the ACF headquarters and reports of police restrictions ahead of the meeting. However, the Board of Trustees subsequently rejected Dalhatu’s purported suspension, describing the decision as illegal and unconstitutional and an attempt to destabilise the northern socio-cultural organisation. item.title: 2027: Stakeholders demand action against electoral violence
item.description: … Falana urges INEC prosecution unit, police warn politicians against sponsoring thugs By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Stakeholders have called for stricter enforcement of electoral laws, prosecution of offenders and accountability for political actors to curb violence ahead of the 2027 general elections. They made the call at the sixth edition of the Frontier Discourse Annual Public Lecture Series and Awards, organised by Pacesetter Frontier Magazine in Abuja on Tuesday, where speakers expressed concern over political thuggery, restrictions on opposition campaigns, unemployment, insecurity and the failure to enforce laws protecting citizens. The event was themed, “Barrel to Ballot: The Naturalisation of Violence, Nigeria’s Polity, and its Democratic Circus.” Delivering the keynote address, human rights lawyer and Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Femi Falana, urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to establish a dedicated prosecution unit to handle electoral offences. He said the commission should obtain reports from the police and other security agencies, investigate electoral violations and prosecute those found culpable. Falana argued that the Electoral Act placed responsibility for prosecuting electoral offenders on INEC, insisting that the commission should not leave the task entirely to the police and other security agencies. He also faulted the National Assembly for failing to implement the recommendation for the establishment of an Electoral Offences Commission, alleging that politicians were deliberately allowing a system that encouraged political thuggery to persist. The senior advocate warned against portraying political violence as the exclusive preserve of any political party, saying supporters of both the ruling party and opposition parties had been involved in attacks. “I am suggesting that INEC should have a prosecution unit with a view to getting reports from the police and other security agencies about electoral offences and then take them to court,” he said. “The politicians in Abuja, members of the National Assembly have refused, deliberately so, to implement the recommendation that there shall be in the country an electoral offences commission. “Politicians do not want to distort the status quo. So they want us to continue to live with thuggery because the thugs are agents of politicians from all the political spectrum.” Falana also alleged that opposition parties had been prevented from erecting campaign billboards in some states, while supporters of different political parties had engaged in acts of vandalism and attacks against their opponents. He insisted that no political party should be allowed to claim innocence or justify violence against its opponents, stressing that all political actors must be held accountable. item.title: Bagudu: With Tinubu’s reforms, prosperity is guaranteed
item.description: Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Senator Abubakar Bagudu, has said the difficult times brought about by President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms are over, paving the way for assured shared prosperity for Nigerians. The minister spoke on Tuesday in Abuja at the media presentation of the All Progressives Congress 2027 presidential election manifesto, themed “From Reforms to Prosperity,” which outlines the Tinubu administration’s policy direction and commitments to translating ongoing reforms into improved living conditions for Nigerians. Bagudu said President Tinubu’s reforms have strengthened private-sector confidence, attracted investment and laid the foundation for inclusive prosperity. He recalled the economic challenges faced by state governments in 2015, when several governors reportedly struggled to meet salary obligations, and contrasted that period with what he described as increased federal allocations, sustained economic growth and improving investor confidence. Bagudu, however, stressed that the ultimate measure of the reforms would be their impact on ordinary Nigerians, particularly hardworking citizens and vulnerable households, and said the next four years of President Tinubu’s tenure will be dedicated to ensuring the people feel the positive impact of the reforms. Also speaking at the presentation, the Chief of Staff to the President, Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila, described the manifesto as a social contract between the government and Nigerians, emphasising that its commitments must be measurable and accountable. He acknowledged the economic pressures of removing the fuel subsidy and implementing foreign exchange reforms, but maintained that the administration’s responsibility was to ensure the gains from reform translate into a better quality of life. item.title: Amaechi Accuses APC Of Dodging Policy Debate, Focusing On Opposition
item.description: The vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Rotimi Amaechi, has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of concentrating on opposition figures rather than presenting its policies and plans to Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general election. Amaechi, a former governor of Rivers State and minister of transportation, said the ruling party was more interested in weakening the opposition than engaging Nigerians on critical national issues. He made the remarks during an interview on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily on Tuesday. According to him, the APC’s campaign rallies have largely focused on attacking opposition figures, particularly him, rather than addressing issues affecting the country. “The party in power is trying to look for how to weaken the opposition; they are scared. Don’t you see their campaign? Tell me one state they have campaigned in that is not about Amaechi; it’s all Amaechi, Amaechi, Amaechi, Ebonyi, Rivers, Amaechi,” he said. ﻿ Policy Debate Amaechi contrasted the ruling party’s approach with the opposition’s campaign, saying his party had focused on issues such as the economy, social housing and security. “When we were campaigning, we were addressing issues. We addressed the issues of economy, social housing, security,” the ex-minister said. Tinubu speaking at a state reception held in his honour at the newly constructed Banquet Hall of ARISE Palm Resort in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, following the APC rally at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, on Friday, November 6, 2026. He further argued that the APC was using his name as a recurring subject at its campaign events instead of explaining what it intended to do if re-elected. “You know what I do every morning? I call my children, [and] I say, ‘You see, your father has achieved so much that he is now the issue in the political discourse of Nigeria.’ NDC is not calling my name because we are in opposition. Anywhere APC is going tomorrow, it’s Amaechi they will mention; they won’t mention what they will do,” he said. View of a market area in Osun State, Nigeria. The former governor also dismissed what he described as the ruling party’s assurances that things would improve in the future, arguing that Nigerians deserved concrete policy proposals rather than promises. “They are not interested; what they are interested in is, ‘don’t worry, things will be better in the future, just put us in power.’ It’s a referendum,” he added. Amaechi contested the ADC presidential primary ahead of the 2027 election but lost to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. He is currently Atiku’s running mate on the party’s ticket. item.title: Anthropic Targets Valuation Of Up To $1.4 Trillion
item.description: Anthropic plans to raise up to $64 billion in its upcoming initial public offering, the artificial intelligence giant said in a filing Tuesday, putting the company’s total valuation at up to $1.4 trillion. The maker of AI agent Claude said in a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission that it aims to sell 825 million shares of Class A common stock at a Wall Street debut price estimate of “between $70.00 and $78.00” per share, amounting to $64.3 billion. Anthropic had been expected to raise up to $100 billion in its IPO, which would have made it the largest IPO on record. The stock market debut is being seen as a gauge of how long the AI spending boom lifting the US economy can last. And it comes as Wall Street is busy digesting the impact of the US midterm elections, in which Democrats won majority control of both chambers of Congress and are vowing to put the brakes on President Donald Trump’s agenda. Anthropic has been aiming to hold its initial public offering the week of November 16. This photograph shows the logo of the US artificial intelligence safety and research company Anthropic displayed on a smartphone’s screen in Brussels on June 10, 2026. Photo by NICOLAS TUCAT / AFP On Monday, the company announced it would release updated versions of two of its most powerful AI models, Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, which it said can perform 30 percent faster than previous versions. Growth has been staggering at the company. Anthropic’s revenue reached $17 billion in the third quarter, up from just $1.4 billion a year earlier, a securities filing showed earlier this month. On Tuesday, the company said its annualized projection, known as the run-rate revenue, “was approximately $81 billion as of October 31, 2026, up $10 billion from September 30.” Estimates in recent months had forecast Anthropic’s valuation at up to a staggering $2 trillion, but the estimates have slipped along with a slide in AI stock prices on Wall Street. Several US media outlets, including The Wall Street Journal and The New York Times on Tuesday estimated the valuation of the company at between $1.3 trillion and $1.4 trillion. item.title: Why an Instagram Following Tracker Can Reveal More Than a Profile’s Follower Count
item.description: A popular Instagram account can attract thousands of followers, but that number rarely tells the whole story. For businesses, content creators, and people researching social media trends, another question can be just as interesting: which accounts does that person choose to follow? Someone may publicly promote fashion, technology, or entertainment while following creators in entirely different fields. A business account may begin following emerging influencers long before announcing a collaboration. A public figure may gradually change the types of accounts appearing on their Following list. These observations can provide useful context, particularly when viewed over time. An Instagram following tracker helps organize changes to the accounts a public Instagram profile follows. Rather than relying on a single snapshot, tools such as Snoopreport record detected follows and unfollows across reporting periods. The results can support social media research, although they cannot explain why someone followed an account or reveal information that Instagram keeps private. Why Follower Counts Don’t Tell the Whole Story Follower numbers are among Instagram’s most visible statistics. They influence how people assess popularity, reach, and sometimes commercial value. Yet having a large audience doesn’t necessarily mean an account has a clearly defined set of interests or strong connections within a particular industry. The Following list offers a different perspective. Consider a technology commentator who starts following several artificial intelligence researchers, software companies, and digital policy organizations. Those additions may suggest topics worth investigating. Similarly, a lifestyle influencer who follows numerous local restaurants might be exploring a new content category. Neither example proves a professional plan or future collaboration. Following someone can reflect curiosity, personal connections, or temporary interest. Still, when researchers compare several observations across time, they may discover changes worth examining further. The Difference Between Following and Followers Before using an Instagram following tracker, it’s important to distinguish two commonly confused terms. Followers are people who subscribe to an account’s updates. Following refers to the accounts that the profile has chosen to follow. For example, a creator may have 40,000 followers while following only 600 accounts. A following tracker focuses on changes within those 600 connections, not on identifying people who recently followed the creator. Instagram allows users to inspect the Following list of an accessible public profile. However, the list doesn’t provide a dependable chronological history of when each connection was added. The order in which accounts appear should not be treated as a reliable record of recent follows. To understand changes, the list needs to be observed across different periods. item.title: What an Instagram Likes Viewer Can Tell Us About the Content People Enjoy
item.description: People reveal different sides of themselves on Instagram. Their profiles may feature carefully selected photographs, polished videos, and short biographies, but their everyday interactions with content can tell another story. A person who rarely posts about travel may regularly like photographs of unfamiliar destinations. A creator known for fashion might engage with technology tutorials, food videos, or sports content. These interactions can suggest topics that attract someone’s attention, even when they don’t appear on the person’s own profile. An Instagram likes viewer can help organize detected likes from public accounts, making it easier to identify recurring content themes rather than examining isolated posts. However, likes are an imperfect signal. They may indicate enjoyment, curiosity, support, or simply a momentary reaction. Understanding their limitations is essential before drawing conclusions. Why Instagram Likes Are So Interesting A like is one of the simplest interactions on social media. It takes only a moment, but it can reflect many different motivations. Someone might like a photograph because they admire the subject, appreciate the photography, support a friend, or agree with a message. For content creators and marketers, likes also form part of the wider picture of audience engagement. A beauty influencer may notice that certain makeup tutorials attract more engagement than product announcements. A restaurant could discover that behind-the-scenes videos generate stronger reactions than ordinary menu photographs. These observations can guide content decisions, especially when combined with comments, shares, reach, and other performance metrics. But there is an important difference between analyzing engagement on your own posts and studying what a particular public account likes elsewhere. Instagram makes the first task relatively straightforward. The second is more complicated. Can You See What Someone Likes on Instagram? Instagram lets users inspect the likes associated with individual posts they can access. For example, if a public photograph has received likes, its visible engagement information may show which accounts interacted with it. What Instagram doesn’t provide is a single public page listing all the posts another person has liked. The platform removed its old Following Activity tab in 2019. That feature previously offered a window into some activities of accounts people followed. Today, users can still explore publicly visible interactions, but building a comprehensive history of another account’s likes is not a standard Instagram feature. This is why an Instagram likes viewer is different from simply opening a photograph and checking its engagement.
